COVID update: Bay Area Aesthetic Surgery has updated their hours and services. 105 reviews of Bay Area Aesthetic Surgery "First off, I need to say I have not had Dr. Beck do surgery on me and since this is a review of him I have given 4 stars. I took one off for his staff and facility. Dr. Beck was awesome. He charges a fee for a consult which is standard with most plastic surgeons, but applies if you have work done. While there he told me straight up about what he thought about my options for facelift, etc. My quote was way beyond what Dr. Vistnes gave me and for less surgical procedures. He has a separate person in his facility that does the light procedures etc and she's very nice but I was distracted by her immense over collagenated lips the whole time I was talking to her. Ducklips is not an overstatement. I kept asking myself if Dr. Beck did that to her... The facility is filled with older furniture, and there are no available before and after photos of patients. (I was surprised and when I asked about it they told me to ask him directly to see if he had any I was like ??? huh ???) The staff ..sigh.. well lets just say they were unorganized and it was a lot like getting an oil change done. They tried to be nice but it seemed like none of them could stand it there. They were not used to being asked a lot of questions about things and not one of them seemed to be running things in the front office. I decided on a whim to go ahead and have him do Botox. I had asked the girl and she said it was 200 an eye. He came in and did some shots on me. (by the way, he did a PERFECT job on the botox) When I went to leave the front desk girl was very curt and just rang up charges on a little machine without talking to me. (I'd planned on getting his recommended skin care products) She charged me the money for the visit, and I had to remind the girl that I got the shots. Then she was very flippant and reversed the visit charge and entered $600 into the little machine. (that's WITH the $100 credit for the visit) I almost fell over! I said, I thought it was 200 per eye? She said, well..he charges by how much he uses, and then pointed to a piece of paper written in chicken scratch with a bunch of technical language and said, "see this is how much he used." Which meant nothing to me. She then pulled out a tiny reciept off the machine and slapped it (literally) on the counter and put her head back down. I stood there for a minute. All this happened so fast, I was still waiting for them to talk to me about the skincare products.... I was in shock at the final cost, that it wasn't explained to me clearly and mostly at how everyone was so aggitated and unorganized. I felt like somehow I'd been taken for something but didn't know what... I was thinking that somehow I was going to get some kind of a real receipt other than a gas station style one. I stood there a couple seconds longer. The girl looked back up at me .. They were supposed to book me for a light pulse facial. I'd been there for an hour and a half already, most of it waiting on someone other than the Dr. I finally just turned around and walked out. It was my first plastic surgeon visit ever. I was underwhelmed to say the least. Dr Beck is handsome and very convincing but if his support staff is so awful something is wrong in Denmark. Since I planned on getting 3 quotes, My next visit was with Dr. Vistnes. It was like night and day. The difference was striking in not only the staff, but the approach to new patients and the facilities. In addiiton, his quote was so much more what I expected in terms of costs. Better facilities, more experienced dr., nicer staff, and less expensive pretty much made me realize that my experience at Bay Area Aesthetic Surgery was not what I had to put up with. I am still looking for a 3rd quote but I will not go back to Dr. Beck except for Botox or other in-office treatment. I am terrified of how I would be treated as a patient there. I shiver at the thought"

I have been a patient of Dr. Norman Lavin's for about 10 years now. He literally saved my life!!! I have a very rare disease that was causing my health and function to seriously deteriorate over a span of about 2 years, and NO other doctors were able to figure out why--for almost 2 years, I had numerous hospital stays and even a long, horrible nursing home stay before I was referred to Dr. Lavin. He never gave up on me! He knew which scans, labs, etc. to order for me, and now I am finally being treated for the disease almost 10 years and have as much of my life back as I can. (There is no cure for the disease, but at least the treatment is helping me live my life.) I am sad to see all the negative reviews here on Yelp. I have NOT had most the experiences described here--I usually have wait times of maybe up to 10 minutes, just like I do at most my other doctors' offices. If I had to choose between shorter wait times or shorter visits with the doctor, well, I think it's more important that Dr. Lavin spends the time with each patient that they need, so I don't mind waiting. And just like with other doctors, I have found that if you can educate yourself the best you can about your condition and be super proactive while you are with the doctor (write down all questions you have for the doctor and bring to your appointment, speak up, find out what your most recent labs/scans show and ask him to explain it to you, etc.), you will have a more positive experience with him. I remember only one occasion I had an appointment with Dr. Lavin when I had looked down briefly and when I looked back up, he was gone--so I went to the front desk and asked them to chase him down for me because I wasn't done with him yet, LOL--and they did, and by the time I left, I felt confident that I had gotten everything I needed from the doctor that day. Dr. Lavin really does have a heart of gold. He really does care about his patients. The nutritionist Kristine has a heart of gold, too, and she is super smart! She will spend as much time as needed getting answers for you, even after she has left for the day--she is also awesome in that she doesn't give up on you. As far as the front desk is concerned, Randi is the person to talk to (I think she's the office manager) if you have any questions, concerns, issues, etc., though you might need to wait till she's off the phone--she and the rest of the staff spend a LOT of time on the phone because they are speaking to your insurance company, your pharmacy, etc. which can be a huge time suck, but that part is not their fault. Randi has worked for Dr. Lavin a long time--she was there when I first became a patient 10 years ago, and she is very knowledgeable and she also has a heart of gold and cares about the patients. My first 5-7 years coming to Dr. Lavin's, the other front desk staff were the same, too--very helpful, kind, efficient, you know their names and they know you when they see you, but I have also noticed that only in the past few years, most of them are gone and now there are new faces, I don't know all of them, they don't know me, and it can be frustrating every once in a while. I, too, have found that sometimes it is hard to get ahold of them on the phone, but that is also true of some of my other doctors' offices. But in the end, it is all offset by getting to see a doctor who is so smart he probably graduated top of his class, who is smarter than pretty much any other doctor around here, and who is smart enough to figure out how to help me when no one else could.

A patient once asked me if I was a good doctor. Nonplussed, I answered that my MOTHER thought I was. Talking about myself is not easy - self-effacements and understatement are values much emphasized in my background. 

I was born in (then colonial) Malaya of Chinese ancestry. I was educated in an American missionary school with an English curriculum and entered medical school at The University of Malaya, graduating in the top quartile of my class. I moved to the United States in 1952 and now live in Claremont with my husband Michael, my stepdaughter Jessica, and a Golden Retriever. 

My Family Practice: 

At first I could not decide, but later I found that it picked me. I enjoy both the arts and science, and Family Practice is a challenging mix of both. I have often called it the liberal arts within the faculty of medicine. It has given me the balanced lifestyle and I enjoy the diversity within the scope of family medicine. I am multi-lingual, fluent in English, Malay and Chinese(Cantonese, Hokkien and Teochew dialects). 

What I enjoy: 

* Educating patients - making the science understandable and applying it to the uncertainties of real life and real people. 

* Laser applications for skin health - hair removal, vein treatments, skin rejuvenation and cosmeceuticals. 

* Holistic medicine and alternate therapies. 

* My office colleagues - The office manager, Lynn Torrez and the other doctors I work with at the Chaparral Medical Group Bonita office - all strong people with integrity and intelligence. It is a real pleasure to work with them. 

* I love art museums, calligraphy, the movies - David Lean and Merchant-Ivory movies, traveling, zoos, the old Tate in London, Singapore, Malayan cooking, tropical gardens, my family, The Galapagos, cooking, painting, walking along the colleges in Claremont, and the Sunday Farmer's Market in the Village in Claremont. 

* I enjoy new things, there isn't enough to learn everything that I want to learn.

Yellowbrick has established a trauma informed clinical philosophy and treatment model, which integrates psycho-neurobiology, developmental psychology and in-depth psychotherapy. 

Psycho-neurobiology focuses on the process of relationships and subsequent development of self-regulation functions. These experiences affect the structural patterning within the brain throughout life. It is a difficult journey, often including many ups and downs, progress followed by setbacks - but if the young adult is serious about moving forward, is honest in their treatment, these setbacks are part of the learning process, part of discovering a new way to live. Dr. Sandeep Bansal is board certified in Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine. He has extensive training and experience in minimally invasive pulmonary procedures including electromagnetic navigational bronchoscopy, bronchial thermoplasty, thoracic ultrasound (endobrochial and chest sonography), argon plasma coagulation, cryotherapy, airway stenting and indwelling pleural catheters for recurrent and malignant pleural effusions.

He has been instrumental in developing a comprehensive lung center in rural Central Western Pennsylvania that allows a rapid assessment and demand management of healthcare needs based on the population characteristics and available resources. The model has been very successful in increasing the availability of advanced pulmonary services including latest technology and population health services such as a robust lung cancer screening program to support the clinical needs in the region.

Dr. Bansal is known for his excellent bedside manners, professional honesty and compassionate attitude towards his patients. He envisions a rapid growth in the field of interventional pulmonary medicine and molecular technology to address the considerable unmet clinical needs of the field especially around the early detection and treatment of lung cancer.

The health care industry is plagued by several issues today.  These include but are not limited to physician shortages, excessive unnecessary care and lack of transparency, all of which result in large amounts of money wasted in the health care field.  These problems can be amplified if you live and practice in rural areas and patients are required to spend several hours traveling to receive essential and basic care.  Patients can be lost in the shuffle of big city health care, which can sometimes result in negative outcomes and an overall stigma that quality healthcare is unattainable. 

Our highly skilled team uses the comprehensive lung care model to increase access to care, affordable screenings, subsequent treatments, access to advanced technology to bring quality health care to a large area of Central and Western Pennsylvania.  We believe in the fact that early adoption of innovative therapies for lung diseases coupled with personalized treatments can save lives, improve quality of life and potentially reduce the health care expenditure.

Every patient deserves the best quality of care.  Care that is affordable, patient centered, individualized and built on evidence based medicine, innovation and leadership in the healthcare and technology field.

text:
Looking for an ENT? Just don't.
I've been dealing with sinus issues for many years and a family member suggested a balloon rhinoplasty to open my passages. The doctor was nice, however I felt like the procedure was somewhat pushed on me upon my first visit -- no alternatives except for gutting out my sinuses, which is a more evasive procedure. I agreed and it was scheduled. I was told that the outpatient procedure would take me out of work for an avg of 2 1/2 days. Although I haven't had any issues post-op, I wish I wouldn't have been awake for what I witnessed after I was numbed up. 
If you're non-religious, then you should know that he'll ask to say a prayer prior to the procedure. He then pulled in 3 other people into that small room to observe (although one 'observer' assisted), and let's just say that it wasn't a walk in the park. He grinds a tube between your canine teeth and your gums to allow the balloon to enter your sinuses, but they don't tell you about the CRUNCH that occurs once the balloon is inflated. Personally, I don't like people messing around in my skull when I'm awake except for my dentist! 
The billing fiasco is another story all together. During the procedure the doctor said that there's no charge for the followup. Upon scheduling, the person on the line said that there is no followup to the procedure (yet they do this to charge your insurance as a regular visit.) Remember when I wrote that the doctor said 'no charge'? They charge your insurance either way and you have to pickup the remainder. So it's really a deferred charge. They said that it's a courtesy that they don't have you pay a copay upon arrival and that they bill your insurance first to see if they'll cover it. The doctor shouldn't say something as stupid as 'no charge' when he doesn't know how his billing works. The bill was only $25, but it's the principle of the matter, you know.
I won't be stepping foot back into this office. I don't care if they gave me a free t-shirt -- I'm burning it!

I have been practicing for 18 years and can't believe how fast time has gone. I took over my practice from David Anzaldua and it was the first Integrative practice in Peoria before it was cool. Patients tell me that the biggest reason they came to my practice was for my diagnostic skills and because I never give up trying to find a cause and a successful treatment. Puzzles don't scare me and in fact are what make me look forward to every day in practice. But I also am a firm believer that prescription medications are not the answer for everything. Common sense is becoming also a proven fact that the pillars of health are good nutrition from whole, clean food, plenty of water, regular daily exercise and good sound sleep. However, I am also human and understand that life can get in the way but we just need to get back on track. Our physical health is also just a part of our health and our spiritual, emotional and mental health are just as important. 

My training has been very focused on holistic health and I'm also a member of the American Academy of Environmental Medicine. Environment plays a huge role in what we're exposed to and even effects how are genes will carry out their instructions. You can't pick your parents but you are also a unique individual and can overcome more than you think. I prefer to be positive and find negativity to be toxic but I can lend an ear when someone is in a dark place and try to help them see there is still hope. 

I am interested in gardening organically, edible landscaping and I'm also a master gardener intern. I love running, biking and swimming and even completed an Ironman. I have a wonderful husband, daughter and step son that also keep me busy and we often go to Chicago on the weekends where we have a condo near Wrigley Field, the home of our beloved Cubs. Recently, I've been learning art from Jeanna Fearon, a local artist and art therapist. She has taught me appreciation for whatever your artistic expression may be and also how to let go and just express yourself. This was very therapeutic for me after my father passed away at almost 98 years of age in 2013 and my mother's health has began to decline. I'm an only child and will not have an easy time when my mom passes but enjoy her continued presence in my life and hope she'll be here still for awhile. She currently lives across the street and turns 90 next year. She's a tough woman despite her small size and has a solid faith in God that serves us all well. 

My biggest concerns for the future of medicine is how rapidly we've had to assimilate the electronic medical record system and the separation of office and hospital medicine and how that will all have to integrate to still care for people and help them efficiently and hopefully improve their health not deter it.

My philosophy of care is also called "feminist medicine" but actually has nothing to do with your gender. It means that instead of telling my patients what to do, I educate them as best as I can and try to understand their unique needs and then we make decisions together. In addition, my style of medicine is to try the least risky and invasive approaches first and then go from there. So if you present with an acute musculoskeletal injury (like back pain) I would recommend chiropractic or therapy first and consider the least addictive medicines if still necessary and if that isn't working we try procedures but try to avoid surgery unless absolutely necessary. 

I did a fellowship in Women's Health that trained me further than Internal Medicine especially with regards to Hormonal Health. So I've got additional expertise in polycystic ovarian syndrome, Menopause,  thyroid disorders, Diabetes Mellitus, adrenal fatigue, and also Functional Medicine.  I have also done research in Fibromyalgia, Migraines, Chronic Pain and Osteoporosis. I thought when I first started I would be seeing mostly women but found that many women wanted me to see their husbands as well. I also took over Dr. David Anzaldua's practice that had focused on sports medicine and so I still see many recreational athletes and men with testosterone deficiency. I try my best to take care of as much of my patient's needs as possible because I do see that patients that collect a lot of physicians are often on more than 10 or 15 medications and often are having more interactions then they realize. But obviously we still need specialists for colonoscopy, surgery when needed and when certain disease states emerge we will need help from subspecialties and thankfully have great ones in Peoria. It's just important to have your primary care doctor involved so that someone knows you very well. 

I was always interested in gynecology and did extra training in my fellowship so in addition to pap smears, I also do endometrial biopsies, simple cystometry, wet/koh prep for vaginitis, IUD placement/removal, subcutaneous contraceptive placement and removal. Before David Anzaldua turned his practice over to me he also trained me in internal and external hemorrhoid treatment, trigger point injections and toenail removal. I also did a plastic surgery rotation and enjoy doing skin biopsies to diagnose benign conditions and rule out malignant conditions. In addition, I am a licensed massage therapist and did additional training in manual lymph drainage. 

I suspect many of the less than excellent reviews came during our transition to EMR.  At the same time discovered that my staff were not making the transition and not helping with patient care. In 2010  I had to let everyone go and start over. I have consistently heard in the past 4 years rave reviews of my nurse Jessica that could draw blood out of a rock and my medical assistant Ian that is so efficient and professional that he's the best assistant I ever had. I also have had excellent feedback for our chiropractic physician, Dr. Ben Miles, he is very gentle and prescise. Our PT, Dr. Korrin Begy doesn't just care for my patients but also gets outside referrals because of her excellent reputation. Ame Nguyen, LMT focuses her treatment using myofascial release and manual lymph drainage to address many medical problems that are chronic and not responsive to many other approaches. I also run closer to on time than many others and have been given good feedback to my face.

However, if you are just seeking pain medications then I'm not your doctor. On another review site I saw that some of my negative reviews were patients I terminated our relationship due to drug deversion or abuse of staff. Life is to short to continue toxic relationships in every avenue of your life.

I knew I wanted to be a Cardiologist when I was 3 years old. I read a book about the heart, and the rest, as they say, is history. 

Cardiology is my passion, and it shows in how I approach the specialty. I follow national guidelines to make sure that patients do not receive unnecessary testing. Basically, I treat my patients as I would treat my own family. If you come to see me for issues such as chest pain, shortness of breath, or hypertension, rest assured that I will address those issues and not try to figure out how to do a more lucrative procedure on your leg veins, as some of my colleagues do. I have always valued the quality of care over the quantity of care, which is the direction healthcare is headed, so you can be confident that I am not interested in performing procedures that are neither warranted nor likely to benefit my patients.

I welcome you to come see me for any of your Cardiovascular needs, and you have my word that I will always put your interests at the top and partner with you in providing the best care possible.

To provide the best cardiac care based on evidence-based guidelines, with individual focus on each patient's own set of circumstances.

As a general Cardiologist, I take care of almost any cardiac related condition, other than advanced arrhythmias (irregular heart rhythms) or device implants (pacemaker, defibrillator). If patients need a cardiac or vascular stent, my highly-skilled partner, Dr. Tai, has the expertise to perform these procedures. If patients need procedures related to the electrical system of the heart, I have very close relationships with specialists in the area who I refer patients to.

I perform most Cardiology procedures that a general Cardiologist performs, with the exception of pacemaker implants. As an added skill, I perform almost all cardiac catheterizations via radial artery access (through the artery in the wrist), which minimizes the complications that can be experienced when having the same procedure done through the artery in the groin, thereby leading to better patient outcomes and satisfaction. I also have advanced training in Echocardiography, including transesophageal echocardiography.

text: I injured both knees two years ago, training for a marathon.  I always dreamed of running an ironman triathlon but suffered from chronic injury.  I made another attempt recently yet I could not handle even small amounts of running.  Both knees did not recover.  I found myself unable to run even for 5 minutes.  It felt hopeless and I was convinced that I was just not going to be able to run at all.  Despite stopping running, the pain did not get better.  I was worried that I would need surgery.  I am a physician and despite my medical training and experience with running, became extremely frustrated with myself, the injuries, and lack of good guidance.  I looked for an orthopedic surgeon who had experience with athletes.  I did not just want to be able to walk pain-free.  I wanted to run and ride my bike as often as I wanted.  I found Dr. Stetson's office.  When I walked into the office, I noticed all the large autographed pictures of olympic athletes on the walls.  I had come to the right place.  Dr. Stetson took my athletic endeavors seriously and I was happy that he did not write me off and say to give up on running.  An MRI showed a small injury to the medial meniscus and some arthritis under the patella.  Dr. Stetson said we should see if we can improve this with conservative measures and physical therapy.  I was appreciative of this conservative approach and felt better that we had a plan.  The subsequent few months were difficult.  I felt that I was making zero improvement.  I found out I had some major muscle weaknesses that were contributing to my pain.  I was neither running nor cycling, just doing therapy.  I kept doing the exercises.  By the beginning of the new year I started to notice some improvement.  I continued physical therapy on my own and learned to run again.  This is a hard part of recovery and requires persistence and retraining the way the brain and the muscles communicate.  I started running 5 minutes at a time.  10 minutes at a time the next week, and so on.  Dr. Stetson saw me from time to time and encouraged me to be patient.  I began to alternate swimming, cycling, and running.  I slowly progressed.  I still had pain from time to time but I felt that I wanted to give triathlon another try.  By this point I had built a small group of experts who got to know me and supported me: Dr. Stetson's team, the physical therapists at Core Conditioning, Lisa the massage and ART specialist at LA bodywork, and my training coach.  I began to struggle again with pain.  Dr. Stetson was confident we could get the pain under control.  His bedside manner is exemplary and he always remembered me.  He made good decisions.  I turned a corner last winter and was able to achieve up to 4 hour bike rides.  Soon thereafter was able to run for 2.5 hours at a time.  I was not certain if I was going to complete the ironman distance but I was happy, just happy being active.  As I got to within 1 month of the race, I developed some swelling behind my left knee and some snapping in the hamstring tendon.  Stephanie the PA saw me with no notice and was able to rule out any serious problem which reassured me that I was going to be ok.  In July, I completed my first ever Ironman triathlon: 2.4 mile swim, 112 mile bike ride, and a 26.2 mile run.  I had a fantastic race and finished the event with no problem.  Not only did I finish but I was able to run the entire marathon.  It was an unbelievable journey of pain and frustration where I went from not being able to run nor bike and then in 2 years finish an ironman with no pain.  I cannot tell you how good it felt to cross that finish line.  I returned a week after my race to Dr. Stetson's clinic to get an MRI of the knee and it was normal.  I learned so much from this experience.  Most importantly I learned that it takes an incredible amount of patience, knowledge, and support from many different people to help you through an injury.  While it may not be possible for everyone to run an ironman, people can and often do more than they believe they can.  People deserve to be able to move their bodies without pain and to have good doctors that they trust absolutely.  Dr. Stetson was in my corner from day 1.  I walked into his office and was prepared for him to tell me I needed surgery.  And I trust Dr. Stetson to operate on me.  In the beginning I was feeling very impatient.  I wanted a magic bullet to just make things normal.  Unfortunately life and the human body does not work so easily.  I have come to appreciate that what truly makes a surgeon great is not just performing successful operations, but also having the knowledge and experience to know when to not operate.  I appreciate that Dr. Stetson had the patience to guide me even when I did not.  A big heartfelt thank you to Dr. Stetson, Stephanie, the medical students, and the entire staff at Stetson Powell Orthopedics sports medicine clinic.  Thank you for helping me make a dream come true.

I am a board certified interventional cardiologist. My primary goal is the care of the patient. I try to treat them as if they were family. 

I went into medicine because I loved science and because of an illness in the family that let me see how important a physician can be in someone's life.

I attended medical school at the Boston University School of Medicine and completed my Internal Medicine residency and fellowships in Cardiovascular Disease and Interventional Cardiology at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, a major teaching hospital of Harvard Medical School.

Since then, I have been a practicing interventional cardiologist at Gwinnett Medical Center. I specialize in radial artery catheterization, a procedure in which I use the wrist artery, rather than the groin artery, to perform cardiac catheterization. This is associated with higher patient satisfaction, lower bleeding risk and hospital costs and shorter hospital stays than the use of the groin artery. In patients having a heart attack, this has even been associated with a lower risk of death.

I also enjoy advanced procedures that allow us to open chronic total occlusions, or total blockages of the arteries that feed the heart. Many patients with such blockages have been told there is nothing that can be done for them other than open heart surgery, and so they suffer from easy fatigue, shortness of breath and chest pains. Emerging technologies now allow us to open these blockages without the need for surgery.

Finally, I love to learn, teach and pass along knowledge to younger physicians. I have taken an active teaching role with the growing Internal Medicine residency program at Gwinnett Medical Center.

My philosophy is patient centered. I strive to put the patient's health, comfort and goals first. I specialize in radial artery catheterization, using the small artery in the wrist to perform coronary angiograms and interventions. This is associated with a lower risk of bleeding, shorter hospital stay and improved patient comfort, allowing the patient to sit up immediately after the procedure. I am board certified in internal medicine, cardiovascular disease and interventional cardiology. My interests lie in taking care of patients with a broad range of cardiovascular conditions, but I have a particular interest in coronary angioplasty and stenting and advanced percutaneous techniques for chronic total occlusions and structural heart disease, including aortic stenosis, atrial septal defects and patent foramen ovales.

I specialize in radial artery catheterization. Rather than using the large artery in the groin, I use the small artery in the wrist to perform cardiac catheterization. I do this for a number of reasons, not the least of which is patient comfort. Large studies have shown that radial artery catheterization is associated with:

1) Improved patient satisfaction

2) Shorter hospital stay

3) Lower risk of bleeding

4) Lower cost

5) In patients having a heart attack, a lower risk of death.

One of my other interests is the treatment of patients with chronic total occlusions, or long-standing total blockages of the arteries that feed the heart. Such patients frequently have low quality of life, including fatigue, shortness of breath and chest pain and have been told there's nothing that can be done for them short of surgery. Emerging technology now allows us to open these total blockages without the need for open heart surgery.

Dr. Bhupendra CK Patel is a Plastic, Reconstructive, and Cosmetic Surgeon. He has been serving in Utah for more than 35 years. Prof. Patel did extended postgraduate fellowships in Europe and in the United States and trained with some of the best surgeons in the world. Prof. Patel's expertise is in the management of disorders involving eyelids, periorbital tissues, lacrimal system and facial bones including fractures and in all cosmetic procedures of the face. He has designed and refined several surgical procedures and instruments. His clinical research interests include thyroid disease, optic nerve disorders, orbital and eyelid tumors, blepharospasm, lacrimal surgery and facial cosmetic surgery.He has developed and published many cosmetic facial surgical procedures, including procedures for the brows, upper and lower eyelids, cheeks and the lower face and neck.The division has been a pioneer in research and development of techniques for the management of ocular and facial disorders, orbital malpositions, thyroid eye disease, optic nerve surgery, lacrimal problems and tearing, eyelid and orbital tumors, and the treatment of orbital and facial fractures. The division developed the use of Botulinum toxin which is also used in the treatment of facial wrinkles and frown lines.Many of the cosmetic and reconstructive surgical procedures utilized have been developed by the division including ptosis repair, upper blephs, endoscopic brow elevation, transconjunctival lower blephs, modified face and neck lifts and fat grafts to the face for cosmetic and reconstructive purposes. Small incision endoscopic brow elevation and midface lifts allow aesthetic improvement in many patients who previously would not have been candidates for surgery. Procedures including chin and cheek augmentation and facial liposculpture are directed at restoring, and enhancing the architecture and support of the face and eyelids procedures that remove supportive structures are avoided.

We have developed numerous surgical techniques in cosmetic and reconstructive surgery which are taught to surgeons the world over. Particular contributions include advanced techniques in endoscopic brow lifts, cosmetic upper and lower blepharoplasty, a unique way to perform mid face lifts, and our techniques of facelifts which gives very natural results, for which patients come to us from all over the world.

Blepharospasm patients are treated with our unique approach withf botox and dysport, and we have modified the surgical approach to give an improvement in the spasms, whilst maintaining an excellent cosmetic outcome. 

Our thyroid patients are treated with especial care since the change in the appearance of the face bothers all our patients. We design surgical techniques individually: using our described technique of orbital decompression and soft tissue repositioning, we obtain excellent results for which patients come to us from all over the world. 

Our approach: perfection!

Being trained in general surgery, plastic surgery, ophthalmology and facial and orbital plastic surgery with further training in lacrimal, eyelid and socket surgery led to one of the longest training periods undertaken by any surgeon at the University (and indeed anywhere!). This gives us a unique perspective to presenting problems, and also provides options to patients that are available because of the wealth of this training and careful attention to detail. 

We frequently see patients for second, third and fourth opinions! We provide opinions to patients seeking such opinions, as well as to other surgeons who ask us to see patients from the whole of the United States and overseas. 

For fellow physicians, nurses and medical personnel needing treatments, we make a particular effort to accommodate their busy schedules, as, indeed we do for other patients. If you need to be seen after hours or on a Saturday, we make every effort to accommodate you.

See our hundreds of before-and-after photographs when you come to see us to see what we aim to provide. 

You will see that we have one of the highest ratings on patient survey scores earned through hard work and with an incredible team which includes Jill, Dena, Mike, Patricia, Todd, Megan, Stacy, the incomparable Diana and many others. Not least is the team of experts we surround ourselves with so that, if needed, we have knowledge of the best surgeons and physicians-who happen to be part of our extended team!

We always take feedback into account and regularly make changes in our clinics and surgery: to that end, patients have been delighted with the level of care provided by Prof. BCK Patel and his team, attention to detail and desire to perform superlatively that they observe and experience. 

As we give as much time as is needed by each patients, we will occasionally keep some of our patients waiting a bit! Although we apologize for this, we also remember that when it is our turn, we want the surgeon and his team to take as much time as is necessary to provide us with the best care.

Outside of practicing medicine, I enjoy traveling, especially internationally to experience and learn about the different cultures of our world. I love music and dancing. I enjoy watching and playing sports (I'm a big Michigan Wolverines and Dallas Cowboys fan!). Last but not least, I enjoy checking out new restaurants.

I am thankful and blessed to be married to the love of my life, Andrea. We have a mixed breed puppy, Ramsey, who is like our little "Sour Patch Kid". I love being a pediatrician because it is one of the few careers where you can let your inner kid be free!

My goal is to try and treat each child and family as if they were my own.

text: I have been a patient at Northwest Women's since 2010 and I recently left the practice. I was satisfied with my care before I ever became pregnant and even through my 1st pregnancy in 2015 that was perfectly normal. However, I got pregnant with my 3rd baby summer of 2019 and the pregnancy ended in miscarriage in September 2019. I was really disappointed with how my OB handled the miscarriage in office and in terms of follow up care (or lack there of). I found out via a regular routine ultrasound in the office at 12 weeks that there was no heartbeat and after that my OB very quickly wrapped up the appointment and told me I needed a d&c. She recommneded that I go to a private practice to have it done but left the room without providing any information about the practice (location, phone number) and I had to go into the main nurse area to be like "um hello can someone let me know where I'm supposed to go for this?" The d&c was totally fine and I had them send a chromosomal sample for testing to find out if there was a cause for it, and the d&c doc said they'd send the results back to my OB. After 3 months of waiting I hadn't received a call from my OB to follow up to see how I was doing post miscarriage, which maybe was unrealistic to expect? Nor had I received any follow up info related to my d&c results. Finally I called labcorp and got the results directly through them but also confirmed they'd send them to my OB, which they had. After a few calls to my OB office a nurse finally called me back and said they had my results and my OB would call me within the next few days to review the results. It has been 2 months and she has yet to call me back. I ended up forwarding my d&c results to my fertility specialist who is wonderful and got back to me about them within 24 hours. So after this I decided to leave the practice for a more compassionate and responsive provider. Hopefully my experience is not the norm here and somehow something slipped through the cracks but it was incredibly disappointing and pretty awful patient care. Maybe they have no idea how to handle anything other than simple routine OB and pregnancy care but given the % of women who miscarry I would expect a big practice like this to have MUCH better in office and follow up care regarding miscarriages. It made the whole experience even worse than it already was.

Dr. Dadvand received a degree in fine arts at an Ivy League University. He then completed a rigorous five year training in general surgery, followed by two years training in plastic surgery. Dr. Dadvand then went on to complete a one year fellowship in advanced aesthetic surgery in Beverly Hills. With his fine arts training and extensive surgical background, Dr. Dadvand started his practice in 2007, with the goal of Perfecting the Art of Plastic Surgery.

Dr. Babak Dadvand grew up in Philadelphia. From a very young age he had an understanding of and fascination with the relationship between the arts and sciences. Indeed, when he went on to pursue an Ivy League education at the University of Pennsylvania, he double majored in chemistry and fine arts to further explore these areas. Dr. Dadvand concentrated his fine arts studies in the fields of oil painting and figure sculpture with a particular focus on portraiture. This has in turn served to hone his eyes and understanding of the human form, which was accentuated by his study of human anatomy in medical school. Dr. Dadvand brings his fine arts background, which above all else gives him a discerning eye when examining patients. He is able to pin point with gentle accuracy facial as well as body features that may be enhanced through his talents.

Dr. Dadvand graduated Magna Cum Laude from the University of Pennsylvania and was further recognized for his outstanding achievements by being named a member of Phi Beta Kappa.

Dr. Dadvand went on to medical school at the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine where he was drawn to the surgical specialties. After earning his doctorate of Medicine (MD) he went on to the prestigious Cleveland Clinic Foundation where he completed a full General Surgery training program. He excelled both clinically and academically, with multiple publications upon completion of his training.

Dr. Dadvand passed both the written and oral examinations to become Board Certified by the American Board of Surgery. He was then accepted to the plastic surgery program at Indiana University Medical Center, a rigorous top-tier program. Here, he honed his skills in all facets of plastic surgery, including cleft-lip/palate repair, head and neck reconstruction, and breast reconstruction. Dr. Dadvand also utilized his time at Indiana University to pursue academic interests, including publications in peer review journals.

Dr. Dadvand drew from years of training and experience during his advanced aesthetic fellowship in Beverly Hills. He knew that all the additional years of training he pursued were necessary to gain true expertise in the field of aesthetic plastic surgery. Dr. Dadvand incorporated his aesthetic training to perform many aesthetic surgical procedures. He also has had extensive training in autologous fat grafting to the face and body, a technique with which most plastic surgeon have limited experience. Dr. Dadvand enjoys all aspects of aesthetic plastic surgery, including facial rejuvenation, nose, breast, and body sculpting work. He has come full circle in incorporating his fine arts background and love for science and uses the latest innovations in plastic surgery to obtain the best results for his patients.
